name: sudo
description: Executes a command with the privileges of another user (usually root), authenticated with your own password and controlled by the sudoers policy.

flags.description: Simulate an initial root login (full root environment).
Run a root shell with the current environment.
Run as another user instead of root.
List the commands you are allowed to run.
Shell history idiom: sudo !! re-runs the previous command with sudo.

examples.explanation: Runs the package index update as root. Your password is requested once and cached for ~15 minutes.
You typed apt install htop and got "Permission denied" — sudo !! re-runs it as root. A beloved shell trick.

examples.output:
User user may run the following commands:
(ALL : ALL) ALL
examples.explanation: Shows your sudo rights. (ALL:ALL) ALL means unrestricted.
Runs a command as alice rather than root — least-privilege access to another account.
Edits /etc/sudoers safely (syntax-checked before saving). NEVER edit sudoers with a plain editor.

about: sudo policy lives in /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d/. On Debian/Ubuntu, membership in the sudo group grants full rights; on RHEL/Fedora it is the wheel group. sudo logs every command to the journal/auth log, which is why it is preferred over shared root logins.
useCases: Perform administrative tasks from a regular account.
Delegate limited rights to specific users/commands.
Keep an audit trail of privileged commands.
mistakes: Editing /etc/sudoers directly and breaking sudo for everyone — always visudo.
Granting NOPASSWD: ALL casually — it removes the last authentication barrier.
warnings: sudo caches your credentials in memory (~15 min default). On shared machines, run sudo -k when stepping away.
distroNotes: The admin group name differs: sudo (Debian/Ubuntu), wheel (RHEL/Fedora/Arch/SUSE).
